verdict.rationale: Browserbase documents real headless browser sessions with auto-waits, plus a fetch capability that converts any URL into HTML. Together these imply that JavaScript is executed and rendered HTML is returned. However, no evidence explicitly addresses JS-heavy single-page applications or guarantees the returned HTML is the fully rendered post-hydration DOM. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that the fetch/HTML output reflects fully rendered SPA content (post-JS execution and hydration), wait-for-render controls tied to HTML extraction, and independent or hands-on corroboration of SPA rendering.

support.subject: As a developer, I can render JavaScript-heavy single-page applications and get the fully rendered HTML
